Main.sentence: FCA US, LLC , ___E:doing business as U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_name)___ Stellantis North America and known historically as Chrysler ( /ˈkraɪslər/ ___E:KRY-slər U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key)___ ),   is one of the " ___E:Big Three U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Three_(automobile_manufacturers))___ " ___E:automobile manufacturers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automobile_manufacturer)___ in the United States, headquartered in ___E:Auburn Hills, Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_Hills,_Michigan)___ .
It is the American subsidiary of the multinational automotive company ___E:Stellantis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellantis)___ .

Stellantis North America sells vehicles worldwide under the ___E:Chrysler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_(brand))___ , ___E:Dodge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge)___ , ___E:Jeep U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeep)___ , and ___E:Ram Trucks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Trucks)___ nameplates.

It also includes ___E:Mopar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mopar)___ , its automotive parts and accessories division, and ___E:SRT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_and_Racing_Technology)___ , its performance automobile division.

The division also distributes ___E:Alfa Romeo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfa_Romeo)___ , ___E:Fiat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiat)___ , and ___E:Maserati U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maserati)___ vehicles in North America.

The original Chrysler Corporation was founded in 1925 by ___E:Walter Chrysler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Chrysler)___ from the remains of the ___E:Maxwell Motor Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_Motor_Company)___ .
In 1998, it merged with ___E:Daimler-Benz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daimler_AG)___ , which renamed itself DaimlerChrysler but in 2007 sold off its Chrysler stake.

The company operated as Chrysler LLC through 2009, then as Chrysler Group LLC. In 2014, it was acquired by ___E:Fiat S.p.A. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiat_S.p.A.)___ ; it subsequently operated as a subsidiary of the new ___E:Fiat Chrysler Automobiles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiat_Chrysler_Automobiles)___ (FCA), then as a subsidiary of Stellantis, the company formed from the 2021 merger of FCA and ___E:PSA Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSA_Group)___ (Peugeot Société Anonyme).

After founding the company, Walter Chrysler used the ___E:General Motors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Motors)___ ___E:brand diversification and hierarchy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_segmentation)___ strategy that he had become familiar with when he worked in the ___E:Buick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buick)___ division at General Motors.

He then acquired ___E:Fargo Trucks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fargo_Trucks)___ and the ___E:Dodge Brothers Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge)___ , and created the ___E:Plymouth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_(automobile))___ and ___E:DeSoto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeSoto_(automobile))___ brands in 1928. Facing postwar declines in market share, productivity, and profitability, as GM and Ford were growing, Chrysler borrowed $250 million in 1954 from ___E:Prudential Insurance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudential_Financial)___ to pay for expansion and updated car designs.

Chrysler expanded into Europe by taking control of French, British, and Spanish auto companies in the 1960s; ___E:Chrysler Europe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_Europe)___ was sold in 1978 to ___E:PSA Peugeot Citroën U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groupe_PSA#History)___ for a nominal $1. The company struggled to adapt to changing markets, increased U.S. import competition, and safety and ___E:environmental regulation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_regulation)___ in the 1970s.

It began an engineering partnership with ___E:Mitsubishi Motors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsubishi_Motors)___ , and began selling Mitsubishi vehicles branded as Dodge and Plymouth in North America.

On the verge of bankruptcy in the late 1970s, it was saved by ___E:$1.5 billion in loan guarantees from the U.S. government. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_Corporation_Loan_Guarantee_Act_of_1979)___ New CEO ___E:Lee Iacocca U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Iacocca)___ was credited with returning the company to profitability in the 1980s.
In 1985, ___E:Diamond-Star Motors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond-Star_Motors)___ was created, further expanding the Chrysler-Mitsubishi relationship.

In 1987, Chrysler acquired ___E:American Motors Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Motors_Corporation)___ (AMC), which brought the profitable Jeep, as well as the newly formed ___E:Eagle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagle_(automobile))___ , brands under the Chrysler umbrella.

In 1998, Chrysler merged with German automaker ___E:Daimler-Benz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daimler-Benz)___ to form ___E:DaimlerChrysler AG U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DaimlerChrysler_AG)___ ; the merger proved contentious with investors.
As a result, Chrysler was sold to ___E:Cerberus Capital Management U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerberus_Capital_Management)___ and renamed Chrysler LLC in 2007.

Like the other Big Three automobile manufacturers, Chrysler was impacted by the ___E:automotive industry crisis of 2008–2010 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automotive_industry_crisis_of_2008%E2%80%932010)___ .

The company remained in business through a combination of negotiations with creditors, filing for ___E:Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_Chapter_11_reorganization)___ on April 30, 2009, and participating in a bailout from the U.S. government through the ___E:Troubled Asset Relief Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubled_Asset_Relief_Program)___ .

On June 10, 2009, Chrysler emerged from the bankruptcy proceedings with the ___E:United Auto Workers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Auto_Workers)___ pension fund, Fiat S.p.A., and the U.S. and Canadian governments as principal owners.
The bankruptcy resulted in Chrysler defaulting on over $4 billion in debts.
In May 2011, Chrysler finished repaying its obligations to the U.S. government five years early, although the cost to the American taxpayer was $1.3 billion.
Over the next few years, Fiat S.p.A. gradually acquired the other parties' shares.

In January 2014, Fiat acquired the rest of Chrysler from the United Auto Workers retiree health trust, making Chrysler Group a subsidiary of Fiat S.p.A.  In May 2014, Fiat Chrysler Automobiles was established by merging Fiat S.p.A. into the company.
Chrysler Group LLC remained a subsidiary until December 15, 2014, when it was renamed FCA US LLC, to reflect the Fiat-Chrysler merger.
As a result of the merger between FCA and PSA, on 17 January 2021 it became a subsidiary of the Stellantis Group.

The Chrysler company was founded by Walter Chrysler on June 6, 1925,   when the ___E:Maxwell Motor Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_Motor_Company)___ (est. 1904) was re-organized into the Chrysler Corporation.

The ___E:company was headquartered U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highland_Park_Chrysler_Plant)___ in the Detroit enclave of ___E:Highland Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highland_Park,_Michigan)___ ,    where it remained until completing the move to its present Auburn Hills location in 1996.

Chrysler had arrived at the ailing Maxwell- ___E:Chalmers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalmers_Automobile)___ company in the early 1920s, hired to overhaul the company's troubled operations (after a similar rescue job at the ___E:Willys U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willys)___ -Overland car company).
In late 1923, production of the Chalmers automobile was ended.
In January 1924, Walter Chrysler launched the well-received Chrysler automobile.
The ___E:Chrysler Six U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_Six)___ was designed to provide customers with an advanced, well-engineered car, at an affordable price.

Elements of this car are traceable to a ___E:prototype U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prototype)___ which had been under development at Willys during Chrysler's tenure  The original 1924 Chrysler included a carburetor air filter, high compression engine, full pressure lubrication, and an oil filter, features absent from most autos at the time.  Among the innovations in its early years were the first practical mass-produced four-wheel hydraulic brakes, a system nearly completely engineered by Chrysler with patents assigned to ___E:Lockheed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Corporation)___ , and rubber engine mounts, called " ___E:Floating Power U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floating_Power)___ " to reduce vibration.
Chrysler also developed a wheel with a ridged ___E:rim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rim_(wheel))___ , designed to keep a deflated tire from flying off the wheel.
This wheel was eventually adopted by the auto industry worldwide.

The Maxwell brand was dropped after the 1925 model year, with the new, lower-priced four-cylinder Chryslers introduced for the 1926 year being ___E:badge-engineered U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badge-engineering)___ Maxwells.
The advanced engineering and testing that went into Chrysler Corporation cars helped to push the company to the second-place position in U.S. sales by 1936, which it held until 1949.
In 1928, the Chrysler Corporation began dividing its vehicle offerings by price class and function.

The ___E:Plymouth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_(automobile))___ brand was introduced at the low-priced end of the market (created essentially by once again reworking and rebadging the Chrysler Series 50 four-cylinder model).
At the same time, the ___E:DeSoto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeSoto_(automobile))___ brand was introduced in the medium-price field.
Also in 1928, Chrysler bought the Dodge Brothers  automobile and truck company and continued the successful Dodge line of automobiles and Fargo range of trucks.
By the mid-1930s, the DeSoto and Dodge divisions would trade places in the corporate hierarchy.
The ___E:Imperial U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_(automobile))___ name had been used since 1926 but was never a separate make, just the top-of-the-line Chrysler.

However, in 1955, the company decided to offer it as its own make/brand and division to better compete with its rivals, ___E:Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Motor_Company)___ and ___E:Cadillac U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadillac)___ .
This addition changed the company's traditional four-make lineup to five (in order of price from bottom to top): Plymouth, Dodge, DeSoto, Chrysler, and the now-separate Imperial.
On April 28, 1955, Chrysler and ___E:Philco U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philco)___ announced the development and production of the World's First All-Transistor car radio.

The all-transistor car radio, Mopar model 914HR, developed and produced by Chrysler and Philco, was a $150 option on the 1956 ___E:Imperial automobile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_automobile)___ models.
Philco began manufacturing this radio in the fall of 1955 at its Sandusky Ohio plant.

On September 28, 1957, Chrysler announced the first production electronic fuel injection (EFI), as an option on some of its new 1958 car models (Chrysler 300D, Dodge D500, DeSoto Adventurer, Plymouth Fury).

The first attempt to use this system was by American Motors on the 1957 ___E:Rambler Rebel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rambler_Rebel)___ .   ___E:Bendix Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bendix_Corporation)___ 's Electrojector used a transistor "computer brain" modulator box, but teething problems on ___E:pre-production cars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-production_car)___ meant very few cars were made.  The EFI system in the Rambler ran fine in warm weather, but suffered hard starting in cooler temperatures and AMC decided not to use this EFI system on its 1957 Rambler Rebel production cars that were sold to the public.
Chrysler also used the Bendix "Electrojector" fuel injection system and only around 35 vehicles were built with this option, on its 1958 production-built car models.

Owners of EFI Chryslers were so dissatisfied that all but one were retrofitted with carburetors (while that one has been completely restored, with original EFI electronic problems resolved). [citation needed]
The ___E:Valiant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Valiant)___ was also introduced for the 1960 model year as a distinct brand.

In the U.S. market, Valiant was made a model in the Plymouth line for 1961 and the DeSoto make was discontinued in 1961. With those exceptions per applicable year and market, Chrysler's range from lowest to highest price from the 1940s through the 1970s was Valiant, Plymouth, Dodge, DeSoto, Chrysler, and Imperial.

In 1954, Chrysler was the exclusive provider of its Hemi V8 engine in the ___E:Facel Vega U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facel_Vega)___ , a French coachbuilder that offered their own line of hand-built luxury performance cars, coupled with the ___E:PowerFlite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PowerFlite)___ and ___E:TorqueFlite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TorqueFlite)___ automatic transmissions.

The ___E:Facel Vega Excellence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facel_Vega_Excellence)___ was a four-door hardtop with rear-hinged ___E:coach doors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coach_door)___ that listed for US$12,800 ($139,501 in 2024 dollars  ).
In 1960 Facel Vega introduced the smaller ___E:Facellia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facel_Vega#Facellia)___ sports car to capitalize on their sales success with Chrysler supplied engines.
At the time, Chrysler didn't produce a four-cylinder engine, and the company had to find alternatives before production began.

In 1960, Chrysler became the first of the "Big Three" automakers to switch to ___E:unibody U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_frame#Unibody)___ construction for its passenger cars, with the exception of Imperial, which continued to be produced on the ___E:body-on-frame U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body-on-frame)___ platform prevalent in the US until 1967, when the unibody construction had proven itself to be reliable enough that Chrysler was willing to also apply it to its flagship.

From 1963 through 1969, Chrysler increased its existing stakes to take complete control of the French ___E:Simca U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simca)___ , British ___E:Rootes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rootes_Group)___ , and Spanish ___E:Barreiros U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barreiros_(manufacturer))___ companies, merging them into ___E:Chrysler Europe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_Europe)___ in 1967. In the 1970s, an engineering partnership was established with ___E:Mitsubishi Motors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsubishi_Motors)___ , and Chrysler began selling Mitsubishi vehicles branded as Dodge and Plymouth in North America.
Chrysler struggled to adapt to the changing environment of the 1970s.

When consumer tastes shifted to smaller cars in the early 1970s, particularly after the ___E:1973 oil crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_oil_crisis)___ , Chrysler could not meet the demand, although their compact models on the "A" body platform, the ___E:Dodge Dart U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge_Dart)___ and ___E:Plymouth Valiant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Valiant)___ , had proven economy and reliability and sold very well. Additional burdens came from increased US import competition, and tougher government regulation of car safety, fuel economy, and emissions.

As the smallest of the Big 3 US automakers, Chrysler lacked the financial resources to meet all of these challenges. 1975 would be the last year for Imperial, except for an ill-fated attempt at revival in 1981-1983, for its low sales no longer justified it as a separate brand when it didn't offer much over a high-end ___E:Chrysler New Yorker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_New_Yorker)___ .
In 1976, with the demise of the reliable Dart/Valiant, quality control declined.

Their replacements, the ___E:Dodge Aspen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge_Aspen)___ and ___E:Plymouth Volare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Volare)___ , were comfortable and had good roadability, but owners soon experienced major reliability problems which crept into other models as well. Engines failed and/or did not run well, and premature rust plagued bodies.

In 1978, ___E:Lee Iacocca U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Iacocca)___ was brought in to turn the company around, and in 1979 Iacocca sought US government help. Congress later passed the Loan Guarantee Act providing $1.5 billion in loan guarantees.

The Loan Guarantee Act required that Chrysler also obtain $2 billion in concessions or aid from sources outside the federal government, which included interest rate reductions for $650 million of the savings, asset sales of $300 million, local and state tax concessions of $250 million, and wage reductions of about $590 million along with a $50 million stock offering. $180 million was to come from concessions from dealers and suppliers.

Also in 1978, Iacocca offloaded the ailing European operation to ___E:PSA Peugeot Citroën U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groupe_PSA)___ for a nominal $1, taking with it the group's substantial losses and debts which had been dragging the rest of the business down.

After a period of plant closures and salary cuts agreed to by both management and the auto unions, the ___E:Plymouth Reliant and Dodge Aries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Reliant)___ compact was introduced in 1981 on the all-new ___E:Chrysler K platform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_K_platform)___ , which was developed from the ___E:Plymouth Horizon and Dodge Omni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge_Omni)___ hatchbacks, which were introduced in 1978. Chrysler returned to profitability in 1980, repaying the loans with interest in 1983. The Omni/Horizon were first offered with four-cylinder engines provided by Chrysler Europe brand Simca, then Volkswagen, until the all-new Chrysler engineered ___E:Chrysler K engine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_2.2_%26_2.5_engine)___ arrived.
Chrysler had not manufactured a four-cylinder engine since 1933 when the ___E:Chrysler flathead four-cylinder U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_flathead_engine)___ was canceled.

In November 1983, the ___E:Dodge Caravan/Plymouth Voyager U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_minivans_(S))___ was introduced, built on a modified K platform, establishing the ___E:minivan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minivan)___ as a major category, and initiating Chrysler's return to stability.
In 1985, ___E:Diamond-Star Motors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond-Star_Motors)___ was created, further expanding the Chrysler-Mitsubishi relationship.

In 1985, Chrysler entered an agreement with ___E:American Motors Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Motors_Corporation)___ to produce ___E:Chrysler M platform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_M_platform)___ rear-drive, as well as ___E:Dodge Omnis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge_Omni)___ front wheel drive cars, in AMC's ___E:Kenosha, Wisconsin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenosha,_Wisconsin)___ , plant.
In 1987, Chrysler acquired the 47% ownership of AMC that was held by ___E:Renault U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault)___ .

The remaining outstanding shares of AMC were bought on the ___E:NYSE U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Stock_Exchange)___ by August 5, 1987, making the deal valued somewhere between US$1.7 billion and US$2 billion, depending on how costs were counted.

Chrysler CEO ___E:Lee Iacocca U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Iacocca)___ wanted the Jeep brand, particularly the ___E:Jeep Grand Cherokee (ZJ) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeep_Grand_Cherokee_(ZJ))___ that was under development, the new world-class manufacturing plant in ___E:Bramalea, Ontario U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bramalea,_Ontario)___ , and AMC's engineering and management talent that became critical for Chrysler's future success.

Chrysler established the ___E:Jeep/Eagle division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeep-Eagle)___ as a "specialty" arm to market products distinctly different from the ___E:K-car-based U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_K_platform)___ products with the ___E:Eagle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagle_(automobile))___ cars targeting import buyers. [citation needed] Former AMC ___E:dealers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Car_dealership)___ sold ___E:Jeep U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeep)___ vehicles and various new Eagle models, as well as Chrysler products, strengthening the automaker's retail distribution system.

___E:Eurostar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurostar_Automobilwerk)___ , a joint venture between Chrysler and ___E:Steyr-Daimler-Puch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steyr-Daimler-Puch)___ , began producing the ___E:Chrysler Voyager U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_Voyager)___ in Austria for European markets in 1992.

In 1998, Chrysler and its subsidiaries entered into a partnership dubbed a "merger of equals" with German-based ___E:Daimler-Benz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daimler-Benz)___ AG, creating the combined entity ___E:DaimlerChrysler AG U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DaimlerChrysler_AG)___ .

To the surprise of many stockholders, Daimler acquired Chrysler in a ___E:stock swap U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_swap)___  before Chrysler CEO ___E:Bob Eaton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_James_Eaton)___ retired.
Under DaimlerChrysler, the company was named DaimlerChrysler Motors Company LLC, with its U.S. operations generally called "DCX".

The Eagle brand was retired soon after Chrysler's merger with Daimler-Benz in 1998  Jeep became a stand-alone division, and efforts were made to merge the Chrysler and Jeep brands as one sales unit.  In 2001, the Plymouth brand was also discontinued.

Eurostar also built the ___E:Chrysler PT Cruiser U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_PT_Cruiser)___ in 2001 and 2002. The Austrian venture was sold to ___E:Magna International U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magna_International)___ in 2002 and became ___E:Magna Steyr U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magna_Steyr)___ .

The Voyager continued in production until 2007, whereas the ___E:Chrysler 300C U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_300C)___ , ___E:Jeep Grand Cherokee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeep_Grand_Cherokee)___ , and ___E:Jeep Commander U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeep_Commander)___ were also built at the plant from 2005 until 2010. [citation needed]

On May 14, 2007, DaimlerChrysler announced the sale of 80.1% of Chrysler Group to American ___E:private equity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_equity)___ firm ___E:Cerberus Capital Management U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerberus_Capital_Management)___ , L.P., thereafter known as Chrysler LLC, although Daimler (renamed as ___E:Daimler AG U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daimler_AG)___ ) continued to hold a 19.9% stake.
The economic collapse during the ___E:2008 financial crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis)___ pushed the company to the brink.

On April 30, 2009, the automaker filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection to be able to operate as a going concern, while renegotiating its debt structure and other obligations,  which resulted in the corporation defaulting on over $4 billion in secured debts.
The U.S. government described the company's action as a "prepackaged surgical bankruptcy".

On June 10, 2009, substantially all of Chrysler's assets were sold to "New Chrysler", organized as Chrysler Group LLC. The federal government provided support for the deal with US$8 billion in financing at nearly 21%.

Under CEO ___E:Sergio Marchionne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Marchionne)___ , "World Class Manufacturing" or WCM, a system of thorough manufacturing quality, was introduced and several products were re-launched with quality and luxury. [citation needed] The Ram, Jeep, Dodge, SRT, and Chrysler divisions were separated to focus on their own identity and brand, and 11 major model refreshes occurred in 21 months.

The ___E:PT Cruiser U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_PT_Cruiser)___ , ___E:Nitro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge_Nitro)___ , ___E:Liberty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeep_Liberty)___ and ___E:Caliber U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge_Caliber)___ models (created during DCX) were discontinued.
On May 24, 2011, Chrysler repaid its $7.6 billion loans to the United States and Canadian governments.

The US Treasury, through the ___E:Troubled Asset Relief Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubled_Asset_Relief_Program)___ (TARP), invested $12.5 billion in Chrysler and recovered $11.2 billion when the company shares were sold in May 2011, resulting in a $1.3 billion loss.     On July 21, 2011, Fiat bought the Chrysler shares held by the US Treasury.
The purchase made Chrysler foreign-owned again, this time as the luxury division.

The ___E:Chrysler 300 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_300)___ was badged Lancia Thema in some European markets (with additional engine options), giving Lancia a much-needed replacement for its flagship.
On January 21, 2014, Fiat bought the remaining shares of Chrysler owned by the ___E:VEBA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voluntary_Employee_Beneficiary_Association)___ worth $3.65 billion.

Several days later, the intended reorganization of Fiat and Chrysler under a new holding company, ___E:Fiat Chrysler Automobiles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiat_Chrysler_Automobiles)___ , together with a new FCA logo were announced.
The most challenging launch for this new company came immediately in January 2014 with a completely redesigned ___E:Chrysler 200 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_200)___ .
The vehicle's creation is from the completely integrated company, FCA, executing from a global compact-wide platform.  [verification needed]
On December 16, 2014, Chrysler Group LLC announced a name change to FCA US LLC.

On January 12, 2017, FCA shares traded at the New York Stock Exchange lost value after the ___E:EPA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency)___ accused FCA US of using emissions cheating software to evade diesel-emissions tests,     however the company countered the accusations,  and the chairman and CEO ___E:Sergio Marchionne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Marchionne)___ sternly rejected them.  The following day, shares rose as investors played down the effect of the accusations.

Analysts gave estimates of potential fines from several hundred million dollars to $4 billion, although the likelihood of a hefty fine was low.  ___E:Senior U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seniority_in_the_United_States_Senate)___ ___E:United States Senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ ___E:Bill Nelson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Nelson_(politician))___ urged the ___E:FTC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Trade_Commission)___ to look into possible deceptive marketing of the company's diesel-powered SUVs. Shares dropped 2.2% after the announcement.
FCA US would in 2022, plead guilty to a criminal charge of conspiring to defraud the US, to wire fraud, and to violate the Clean Air Act.
On July 21, 2018, Sergio Marchionne stepped down as chairman and CEO for health reasons, and was replaced by John Elkann and Michael Manley, respectively.

In 2007, Chrysler began to offer vehicle lifetime powertrain warranty for the first registered owner or retail lessee.

The deal covered owner or lessee in U.S., Puerto Rico, and the Virgin Islands, for 2009 model year vehicles, and 2006, 2007, and 2008 model year vehicles purchased on or after July 26, 2007. Covered vehicles excluded SRT models, Diesel vehicles, Sprinter models, Ram Chassis Cab, Hybrid System components (including transmission), and certain fleet vehicles.
The warranty is non-transferable.
After Chrysler's restructuring, the warranty program was replaced by five-year/100,000 mile transferable warranty for 2010 or later vehicles.

In 2008, as a response to customer feedback citing the prospect of rising gas prices as a top concern, Chrysler launched the "Let's Refuel America" incentive campaign, which guaranteed new-car buyers a gasoline price of $2.99 for three years.

With the U.S. purchase of eligible Chrysler, Jeep, and Dodge vehicles, customers could enroll in the program and receive a gas card that immediately lowers their gas price to $2.99 a gallon, and keeps it there for the three years.

In March 2011, Chrysler Group LLC filed a lawsuit against Moda Group LLC (owner of Pure Detroit clothing retailer) for copying and selling merchandise with the "Imported from Detroit" slogan.
Chrysler claimed it had notified defendant of its pending trademark application February 14, but the defendant argued Chrysler had not secured a trademark for the "Imported From Detroit" phrase.
On June 18, 2011, U.S.

District Judge Arthur Tarnow ruled that Chrysler's request did not show that it would suffer irreparable harm or that it had a strong likelihood of winning its case. Therefore, Pure Detroit's owner, Detroit retailer Moda Group LLC, can continue selling its "Imported from Detroit" products.

Tarnow also noted that Chrysler does not have a trademark on "Imported from Detroit" and rejected the automaker's argument that trademark law is not applicable to the case.   In March 2012, Chrysler Group LLC and Pure Detroit agreed to a March 27 mediation to try to settle the lawsuit over the clothing company's use of "Imported from Detroit" slogan.
Pure Detroit stated that Chrysler has made false claims about the origins of three vehicles - Chrysler 200, Chrysler 300 and Chrysler Town & Country - none of which are built in Detroit.
Pure Detroit also said that Chrysler's Imported From Detroit merchandise is not being made in Detroit. [citation needed] In 2012 Chrysler and Pure Detroit came to an undisclosed settlement.

The dedicated tank building division of Chrysler, this division was founded as the Chrysler Tank division in 1940, originally with the intention of providing another production line for the ___E:M2 Medium Tank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M2_Medium_Tank)___ , so that the U.S.
Army could more rapidly build up its inventory of the type. Its first plant was the ___E:Detroit Arsenal Tank Plant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Arsenal_(Warren,_Michigan))___ .

When the M2A1 was unexpectedly declared obsolete in August of the same year, plans were altered (though not without considerable difficulty) to produce the ___E:M3 Grant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M3_Lee#Development)___ instead, primarily for the British as part of the United States under the counter support for the United Kingdom against Nazi Germany (the U.S. not yet being formally in the war), with the balance of the revised order going to the U.S.
Army as the Lee .

After December 1941 and the United States' entry into the war against the Axis powers, the Tank division rapidly expanded, with new facilities such as the ___E:Tank Arsenal Proving Ground U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Packard_Proving_Grounds)___ at (then) ___E:Utica, Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utica,_Michigan)___ .

It also quickly widened the range of products it was developing and producing, including the ___E:M4 Sherman tank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M4_Sherman#U.S._design_prototype)___ and the ___E:Chrysler A57 multibank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_A57_multibank)___ tank engine.

During World War II, essentially all of Chrysler's facilities were devoted to building military vehicles (the ___E:Jeep U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeep)___ brand came later, after Chrysler acquired ___E:American Motors Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Motors_Corporation)___ ).

They were also designing V12 and V16 ___E:hemi-engines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemispherical_combustion_chamber)___ producing 2,500 hp (1,864 kW; 2,535 PS) for airplanes, but they did not make it into production as ___E:jets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jet_engine)___ were developed and were seen as the future for air travel. [citation needed] During the 1950s ___E:Cold War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War)___ period, Chrysler ___E:made air raid sirens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_air_raid_siren)___ powered by its Hemi V-8 engines.

When the ___E:Radiation Laboratory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiation_Laboratory)___ at ___E:MIT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology)___ was established in 1941 to develop ___E:microwave radars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microwave_radar)___ , one of the first projects resulted in the ___E:SCR-584 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SCR-584)___ , the most widely recognized radar system of the war era. This system included a ___E:parabolic antenna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parabolic_antenna)___ six feet in diameter that was mechanically aimed in a helical pattern (round and round as well as up and down).
One of Chrysler's most significant contributions to the war effort was in radar technology.

For the final production design of this antenna and its highly complex drive mechanism, the Army's ___E:Signal Corps Laboratories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal_Corps_Laboratories)___ turned to Chrysler's Central Engineering Office.
There, the parabola was changed from aluminum to steel, allowing production to form using standard automotive presses.
To keep weight down, 6,000 equally spaced holes were drilled in the face (this had no effect on the radiation pattern).
The drive mechanism was completely redesigned, using technology derived from Chrysler's research in automotive gears and differentials.
The changes resulted in improved performance, reduced weight, and easier maintenance.
A large portion of the Dodge plant was used in building 1,500 of the SCR-584 antennas as well as the vans used in the systems.
In April 1950, the U.S.

Army established the Ordnance Guided Missile Center (OGMC) at ___E:Redstone Arsenal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redstone_Arsenal)___ , adjacent to ___E:Huntsville, Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntsville,_Alabama)___ .
To form OGMC, over 1,000 civilian and military personnel were transferred from ___E:Fort Bliss, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Bliss,_Texas)___ .

Included was a group of German scientists and engineers led by ___E:Wernher von Braun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wernher_von_Braun)___ ; this group had been brought to America under ___E:Project Paperclip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Paperclip)___ .

OGMC designed the Army's first ___E:short-range ballistic missile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short-range_ballistic_missile)___ , the ___E:PGM-11 Redstone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGM-11_Redstone)___ , based on the WWII German ___E:V-2 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V-2)___ missile.
Chrysler established the Missile Division to serve as the Redstone prime contractor, setting up an engineering operation in Huntsville and for production obtaining use from the U.S.
Navy of a large plant in ___E:Sterling Heights, Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterling_Heights,_Michigan)___ .

The Redstone was in active service from 1958 until 1964; it was also the first missile to test-launch a live ___E:nuclear weapon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_weapon)___ , first detonated in a 1958 test in the South Pacific.

Working together, the Missile Division and von Braun's team greatly increased the capability of the Redstone, resulting in the ___E:PGM-19 Jupiter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGM-19_Jupiter)___ , a ___E:medium-range ballistic missile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medium-range_ballistic_missile)___ .

In May 1959, a Jupiter missile launched two small monkeys into space in a ___E:nose cone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nose_cone)___ ; this was America's first successful flight and recovery of live space payloads.

Responsibility for deploying Jupiter missiles was transferred from the Army to the Air Force; armed with ___E:nuclear warheads U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_warheads)___ , they were first deployed in ___E:Italy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy)___ and ___E:Turkey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey)___ during the early 1960s.

In July 1959, ___E:NASA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA)___ chose the ___E:Redstone missile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redstone_missile)___ as the basis for the ___E:Mercury-Redstone Launch Vehicle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury-Redstone_Launch_Vehicle)___ to be used for suborbital test flights of the ___E:Project Mercury U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Mercury)___ spacecraft.
Three uncrewed MRLV launch attempts were made between November 1960 and March 1961, two of which were successful.

The MRLV successfully launched the chimpanzee ___E:Ham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ham_(chimpanzee))___ , and astronauts ___E:Alan Shepard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Shepard)___ and ___E:Gus Grissom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Grissom)___ on three suborbital flights in January, May, and July 1961, respectively.

America's more ambitious crewed space travel plans included the design of the ___E:Saturn series U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_(rocket_family))___ of heavy-lift launch vehicles by a team headed by ___E:Wernher von Braun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wernher_von_Braun)___ .

Chrysler's Huntsville operation, then designated the Space Division, became ___E:Marshall Space Flight Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Space_Flight_Center)___ 's prime contractor for the first stage of the ___E:Saturn I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_I)___ and ___E:Saturn IB U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_IB)___ versions.

The design was based on a cluster of Redstone and ___E:Jupiter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGM-19_Jupiter)___ fuel tanks and Chrysler built it for the ___E:Apollo program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_program)___ in the ___E:Michoud Assembly Facility U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michoud_Assembly_Facility)___ in East New Orleans, one of the largest manufacturing plants in the world.

Between October 1961 and July 1975, NASA used ten Saturn Is and nine Saturn IBs for suborbital and orbital flights, all of which were successful;  Chrysler missiles and boosters never suffered a launch failure. [citation needed] The division was also a subcontractor which modified one of the ___E:mobile launcher platforms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_launcher_platform)___ for use with the Saturn IB rockets using Saturn V infrastructure.
